commits.author: atqamar
penfever
commits.message:
[rl] Fail closed when a multi-node RL launch cannot use InfiniBand (#11619)

Multi-node RL jobs request the cluster's InfiniBand fabric, but since
2026-10-20 the Snowball-family recipes have forced NCCL onto TCP
sockets, and one production run died from a socket-transport NCCL error.
The two-node probe in this PR measured the default environment passing
cross-node over InfiniBand on both H100 clusters (85-88 GB/s all-reduce)
and the socket override passing at 19-24x lower bandwidth where it
completes at all; partial overrides hang at IPv6 link-local bootstrap.
This PR makes a launch refuse to run multi-node training on sockets
instead of silently falling back.

Two checks, one per launch stage:

1. Static, at config resolution: the SkyRL launch builder refuses a
multi-node recipe whose `extra_env` sets `NCCL_NET=Socket` or
`NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1`, naming the variables.
2. Live, at task startup: the per-node task shell runs
`nccl_transport_probe.py --mode gate`. Tasks 0 and 1 exchange one
all-reduce and one all-to-all over the default environment on the job's
own allocation (NCCL INIT, transport census, bounded time); the task
fails with the exact NCCL error tail unless the census shows `NET/IB` or
no NET transport (intra-node NVLink, where the socket variables are
irrelevant anyway). The full environment-variant matrix stays available
as the diagnostic mode (`--variants`).

The probe (launcher, worker, and gate modes) ships as
`experiments/post_training/nccl_transport_probe.py`. Measured results
per cluster, including the 02a finding that the three-variable override
alone aborts there and only the production overlay with
`NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` passes: [probe
results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11619#issuecomment-6964135906).
Run provenance and the recipe lineage are recorded in #11618.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[shellbox] Work around Daytona log-stream boundary bugs in processes (#11689)

Daytona `open_process` sessions could stall on, or corrupt, frames in
the bridge's output stream. The Daytona server prefixes every output
line with a three-byte stream marker (`\x01\x01\x01` for stdout,
`\x02\x02\x02` for stderr) and sends the log as 1,024-byte websocket
messages. The SDK's demultiplexer (`daytona/_utils/stream.py`, 0.200.2)
mishandles two boundary cases:

| Message boundary | SDK behavior | Effect on Shellbox |
|---|---|---|
| Final message is 1–2 bytes, e.g. a frame's lone `\n` | Withheld until
more output arrives | Frame stalls until the guest writes again |
| A marker ends exactly at a message boundary | Marker bytes passed
through as output | Frame fails to decode; with stderr active, data can
reach the wrong stream |

The bridge now sends every frame, including stderr and exit frames, on
stdout, each followed by an empty `P` padding frame that the host
discards. Only padding can be withheld, and no stream switch can
misroute data. The host removes `\x01` and `\x02` bytes, which base64
frames never contain, before decoding. The process's stderr still
reaches `ProcessSession.stderr` as `E` frames; Daytona's stderr channel
now carries only startup errors from the image shell or Python.

In the SWE-Bench Pro smoke run, 12 model requests from 4 of 22 sandboxes
reached the host 608 s after the guest sent them, just after the guest
relay's 600 s timeout and the agent's retry. The host answered each in
3–5 s. Retries resent identical bodies, so the same split repeated, and
3 trials ended in `AgentTimeoutError`. A live reproduction sent lines of
random sizes through `open_process`. Two sizes stalled in every sandbox
until the guest wrote again, each ending in a 1-byte message. Adding the
padding alone made marker leaks frequent: a smoke run lost 4 of 22
trials to `Only base64 data is allowed`. Under heavy concurrent stderr,
the unpatched bridge also corrupted 3 of 4 sessions. With this change,
2,400 round trips across 6 sandboxes, with random sizes and concurrent
stderr, completed with no corrupt frames or stalls. The slowest took 2.1
s.

The fake provider in `test_daytona_process.py` now withholds the last
two bytes of output and inserts a leaked marker byte after each line.
The new test fails without these changes.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[shellbox] Add a Daytona quota and usage CLI for sizing concurrency (#11745)

Agents need live capacity numbers to size Daytona launches; a static
quota
table cannot show what other lanes already use on the org. The new
`shellbox-daytona-usage` command reports one account's CPU, memory,
disk,
snapshot and volume quota and current use, sandbox counts by state, and
a
suggested maximum additional concurrency.

The command reads the account's paginated sandbox inventory and the
usage
overview through one API key from an explicit environment variable. The
`/organizations` endpoint rejects API keys with 401, so the command
resolves
the organization ID from the inventory; an org without sandboxes falls
back
to snapshots and then volumes. The concurrency suggestion is the minimum
over
remaining CPU, memory and disk capacity of the quota row for the
launch's
target region and sandbox class, each reduced by a 20% headroom, for a
per-sandbox profile given with `--cpu`, `--memory-gib` and `--disk-gib`.
`--all` sweeps the three known accounts; `--json` emits the
machine-readable
report; per-sandbox requests above the row maxima print a warning.
`.agents/ops/daytona.md` documents the command and the sizing rule.

[eval] Freeze Micro210 policy at the model-binding boundary (#11686)

Keep one frozen Micro210 evaluation protocol so model comparisons use
the same settings. Pin the policy URI, revision, SHA-256 and byte size
in code, and verify those bytes before use. The policy fixes dataset
revisions, selected task IDs and repetitions, sampling, seed, judge,
harness deadlines and execution settings.

The `experiments.evaluation.micro210` entrypoint accepts a model

reject edits to the generated launch YAML. Persist the policy digest
beside the results and retain all evaluation trajectories under the
supplied run identity.

The [human-readable policy

used by the code; tests use a small synthetic policy offline.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[shellbox] Run the Daytona process bridge on Python 3.8 guests (#11666)

The Daytona process bridge now starts on guest images whose `python3` is
3.8. The bridge executes the shared frame codec, `process_framing.py`,
with the image's own interpreter, and that module's `tuple[bytes,
bytes]` return annotation raised `TypeError: 'type' object is not
subscriptable` at definition time before Python 3.9. Postponed
annotations remove the evaluation. The rest of the bridge and the HTTP
relay guest already ran on 3.8, so the README now states 3.8 as the
minimum for `open_process` and the relay listener.

Every Daytona `open_process` failed on such images, including Harbor's
model relay. In a SWE-Bench Pro smoke run, both `protonmail/webclients`
tasks failed at startup with "Model relay failed to start", because that
repository's image ships Python 3.8.

A live Daytona sandbox on `python:3.8-slim-bullseye` reproduces the
failure without this change and serves a relay request with it. CI has
no Python 3.8 interpreter, so the change has no automated regression
test.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[grug] Shard expert RNG at initialization (#11288)

Stacked Grug expert initialization can exhaust TPU HBM before checkpoint
restore because random weights are generated as full replicated arrays
and sharded afterward. Request the existing target sharding when
generating each expert tensor, so RNG temporaries are partitioned too.

An eight-device CPU regression preserves every generated weight
bit-for-bit with partitionable Threefry and reduces compiler temporary
allocation from 50,331,972 to 2,623,236 bytes. The output allocation is
unchanged. On one TPU v4-8 host (4 chips, 30.75 GB HBM each),
initializing 4 stacked layers of 64 experts (hidden 2048, intermediate
4096, ring, expert axis 4) runs out of HBM on main, needing 32.00 GB of
temporaries in `jit_init`. With this change, the same init compiles with
1.00 GB of temporaries and 6.00 GB per chip of output, and two training
steps then run with finite loss.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[sft] Mirror HFModel Hub weights on CPU before training (#11117)

SFT runs that start from a Hub `HFModel` no longer download weights on
the accelerator task. `HFModel` passed its Hub id to
`initialize_from_hf`, and Levanter's `train_lm` loads that id straight
from the Hub, so each GPU or TPU task downloaded the full repo before
training. A Hub ref now adds the existing `download_model` step from
`experiments/models.py` as a dependency. Its Zephyr CPU workers copy the
repo to `models/{repo}--{sha}` under the regional prefix.
`initialize_from_hf` and the default tokenizer then read that copy.
`ConvertedCheckpointModel` and `PreparedModel` already worked this way.
An object-store or local path is still loaded in place, with no extra
step. Hub-vs-path uses Levanter's own rule, now public as
`levanter.compat.hf_checkpoints.is_hf_model_id`, so the launcher and the
loader agree. An `hf://org/model@<sha>` ref names the same commit, so it
gets the same pin check and copy.

A Hub ref must now pin a full 40-character commit (`org/model@<sha>`).
The copy's address is hash-free and includes the sha, so an unpinned ref
would let the same path hold different weights. The Delphi recipe and
the TPU smoke recipe now pin the commit they were loading; Snowball was
already pinned. Delphi and Snowball also drop their unpinned
`tokenizer_path` (the same repo as the weights), so the tokenizer comes
from the pinned copy too. This changes their tokenizer cache key, so
their chat caches rebuild once.

The copy is a durable `models/` artifact rather than Levanter's 30-day
`hf-models` TTL cache. Step records outlive TTL objects, so after expiry
a cached step would point at deleted weights.


The full-sha GCS path already held a copy from an older executor, and
its `.artifact.json` was the bare payload `null`. The old executor wrote
that for every step that returned `None`, so every `models/` download
folder in the GCS buckets has one. `read_record` raised a
ValidationError on it, so the drift check crashed before it could serve
the cache. `read_record` now treats a `null` file as missing and falls
back to the old `.executor_info`, as it already does for folders with no
record. The finished copy is served with no re-download.

The mirror step alone was run for the TPU smoke ref
`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B@c1899de2…` as Iris CPU jobs, with no training. On the
GCP cluster, `ctx.artifact_path` resolved to
`gs://marin-us-central2/models/Qwen--Qwen3-0-6B--c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`,
and the existing copy was served from cache. On `cw-rno2a`, it resolved
to
`s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/models/Qwen--Qwen3-0-6B--c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`,
which is that cluster's `MARIN_PREFIX`. A fresh Zephyr download wrote
that copy. Both roots list the same model files:

```text
config.json               726
generation_config.json    239
merges.txt            1671853
model.safetensors  1503300328
tokenizer.json       11422654
tokenizer_config.json    9732
vocab.json            2776833
```

Design doc: [HF Model Load
Pre-Caching](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-rRhP9mB4hpbzXwxUfPUTejwUVk1w68BOIs9TWdsBFk),
section "SFT".

Part of #9233

commits.author: mminutoli
commits.message:
[grug] Add a dense synthetic harness for Llama-3 8B and Marin 32B shapes (#11124)

Add `experiments/grug/dense_synthetic`, a dense counterpart of the
Snowball synthetic harness, so dense GEMM and attention throughput are
measured on the same footing as the MoE. It uses the same
Levanter-trainer setup, flags and summary lines on a dense model built
from the June 67B Grug blocks: layers under one `lax.scan`, per-block
remat, Grug attention, FSDP and TP layout and June's SwiGLU `DenseMLP`,
with full RoPE and optional per-head QK-norm.

- Presets: `tiny` (CPU check), `8b` (Llama-3 8B) and `32b` (Marin 32B in
Qwen3 layout, QK-norm, untied embeddings); `--layers` gives shallower
proxies.
- `--remat-mode` is `recompute_all`, `save_dots` or `none`;
`--model-axis` adds tensor parallelism; mixed precision defaults to
`p=f32,c=bfloat16`.
- FLOPs per example are Levanter's Llama and Qwen3 counts, so MFU is
comparable with theirs; only process 0 logs the median-step summary.
- The harness opts out of the grug variant contracts (`GRUG NOVERIFY`)
because it drives Levanter's `Trainer`, not the grug template loop.

Stacked on #11123; the last two commits are this PR's.

Tests check preset parameter counts and FLOPs against `llama_8b` and
`llama_32b`, that remat modes keep loss and gradients, and that QK-norm
makes the loss independent of a common `w_q`/`w_k` scale: 7 passed; grug
variant contracts 26 passed.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[evals] Add LongBench v2 with precompiled middle-truncated prompts (#11504)

Add `longbench-v2` and `longbench-v2-thinking`, curated evaluations of
[LongBench v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15204): 503 multiple-choice
questions over contexts of 8,000 to 2 million words. Data is pinned to
[`zai-org/LongBench-v2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/zai-org/LongBench-v2)
revision `2b48e494` (Apache-2.0); the prompt, middle truncation and
answer parser follow
[THUDM/LongBench@2e00731](https://github.com/THUDM/LongBench/tree/2e00731f8d0bff23dc4325161044d0ed8af94c1e)
(MIT). `longbench-v2` runs greedy with thinking off and 4,096 output
tokens. `longbench-v2-thinking` uses the Qwen3.5 model card's
thinking-mode sampling and 32,768 output tokens, without its presence
penalty, which the sampling spec does not express. New catalog entries
serve Qwen3-32B with YaRN at 131K tokens (the leaderboard's setup) and
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B at 262K.

Upstream truncates each prompt to the model's limit at run time. Here
each item is published with its full prompt plus copies cut to a ladder
of `o200k_base` token budgets (8K to 894K in steps of 1.25×, including
upstream's 120K), keeping the first and last halves as upstream does. A
run sends the largest copy that fits the served context and output
budget, so every model answers all 503 items and models at the same
budget see identical prompts. Results are grouped by length, difficulty
and domain. #10234 plans this length-stratified pilot alongside MRCR, to
cover realistic multi-document tasks that MRCR does not.

Full 503-question runs on this branch, in percent accuracy:

| Model | Context | Thinking | Overall | Short | Medium | Long |
Reference | Evaldash |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-32B | 131K, YaRN | off | 38.2 | 46.1 | 33.5 | 34.3 | 38.8
([leaderboard](https://longbench2.github.io/)) |
[run](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/longbench-v2-ts-full-qwen3-32b-20261113-longbench-v2-ede3e57aeb4e59a9aac856aeb41f3476)
|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 262K | off | 52.1 | 57.8 | 49.3 | 48.1 | — |
[run](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/longbench-v2-ts-full-qwen3.5-35b-20261114-longbench-v2-4635a73b6e1b51eea4e265bb7fddd825)
|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 262K | on | 60.8 | 66.7 | 60.0 | 52.8 | 59.0 ([model
card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B)) |
[run](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/longbench-v2-ts-full-qwen3.5-35b-20261114-longbench-v2-thinking-5560e3ef118c52718284fa6d63aa9d29)
|

Qwen3-32B matches the leaderboard, which uses the upstream harness,
within one standard error (2.2 points). An earlier Evalchemy
implementation that truncated to each model's exact limit scored 38.4,
52.5 and 64.4 on the same three runs. The thinking-mode gap is
significant on a paired test (41 items lost, 23 gained) and comes from
two places: 3 points on prompts sent in full, where the only differences
are the missing presence penalty and sampling variation at temperature
1.0, and 5 points on the 113 truncated items, whose ladder copies
averaged 12% shorter than an exact-fit cut. The 120K copy equals
upstream `pred.py` truncation on all 205 prompts long enough to need it.

An audit of the earlier implementation, whose prompt and parser this one
reuses, found prompts identical to upstream on all 503 rows and answer
extraction identical to upstream on 20,000 fuzzed and 1,026 real
responses; two blinded reviewers agreed with the grader on 119 of 120
sampled responses. The grader reads only the final answer: it uses the
`final_only` response selection from #11201, so a response whose final
answer is empty scores zero and its reasoning is never graded.
Re-grading the stored thinking outputs confirmed that no reasoning
reached the grader in the runs above, so the switch leaves their scores
unchanged; the Qwen3.5 profile now names its reasoning parser
explicitly. Responses with no parseable answer score zero: 1, 7 and 10
in the three runs, 16 of them cut off at the output limit. Upstream's
parser reads "The correct answer is Choice B" as C; the grader keeps
that behavior, and strict `xfail` fixtures record it.

Each run on CoreWeave H100s:

| Run | GPUs | Eval time | Start to finish | H100-hours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-32B, thinking off | 2 | 2 h 14 min | 2 h 20 min | 4.7 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, off then on | 4 | 46 + 76 min | 2 h 11 min | 8.8 |

Each run reads 40M to 60M prompt tokens. Compiling the corpus takes
under a minute and stores 277 MB per protocol.

Renaming `ChatPromptVariant.fewshot`, which this importer uses as a
selection rank, is left to a follow-up because it also changes
MMLU-Pro's protocol fingerprint.

Part of #10234.

commits.message:
[shellbox] Retry Daytona sandbox deletion after gateway errors (#11735)

A Daytona sandbox leaks when its deletion hits a transient gateway
error. During task-machine cleanup, the lookup before deletion returned
`502 Bad Gateway`; the cleanup logged `Task-machine provider close
failed` and left the sandbox running until its TTL expired.

Sandbox deletion now retries 502, 503 and 504 responses with backoff
within the existing 10-second interrupt deadline, as the snapshot
metadata lookup already does. A missing sandbox still ends cleanup, and
other errors still propagate. The two call sites share one
transient-status set, renamed `TRANSIENT_DAYTONA_STATUS`.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[rl, iris] Pin NCCL to the InfiniBand rails on CoreWeave H100 clusters (#11749)

Each H100 node on our CoreWeave clusters has two networks: InfiniBand
for GPU-to-GPU traffic and a slower Ethernet network for everything
else. NCCL normally sees only the InfiniBand cards. The Snowball quick
loop runs its pods in privileged mode, which also exposes the Ethernet
card to NCCL. NCCL then sends some GPU traffic over it, that traffic
never reaches the other node, and the job fails with
`IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR(12)`. The InfiniBand fabric is healthy.

This PR sets `NCCL_IB_HCA=ibp`, which restricts NCCL to the InfiniBand
cards (`ibp0`–`ibp7`), and drops the TCP workaround from #11700:

- `lib/iris/config/cw-us-east-02a.yaml`, `cw-rno2a.yaml`: set it in
`task_env` for every job. Takes effect after each controller's config
rollout.
- `train_quick_loop.py`: replace `NCCL_NET=Socket`, `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1`
and `NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY=AF_INET` with the pin. Takes effect at once;
SkyRL forwards `NCCL_IB_HCA` to every Ray actor.
- `lib/iris/docs/coreweave.md`: document the setting and how to check
it.

The workaround puts weight sync on TCP:

| Network | Weight sync per update | Source |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| TCP (current quick loop) | 6.9–9.1 s | #11178 |
| InfiniBand | 0.50–0.54 s | #11178 (`2t8k34cn`) |

A two-node test on cw-rno2a reproduced the failure: forcing NCCL onto
the Ethernet functions failed every transfer with the production error,
and the InfiniBand cards passed every transfer. The node layout,
diagnostic, and evidence are in [Echo wiki
#1026](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/1026).

Limits:

- A quick-loop run over InfiniBand has not been done yet.
- us-west-04a is unchanged because its device names are unverified. A
value that matches no device makes NCCL fall back to TCP silently; check
`NET/IB : Using [0]ibp0 …` under `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[rl-data] Add typed records for licenses, statuses and difficulty (#11568)

The Atlas pipeline needs one contract for its admission decisions. It
now
writes them as typed records, so the catalog app and every campaign
writer
read the same shapes. The records here are the ones the Atlas app needs
to
deploy in Marina's runtime.

finestore gets these record types:
- the license receipt: primary evidence at an immutable pin, with a
derived
  classification and fail-closed admission checks
- the status taxonomy: source statuses, canonical exclusion reasons,
typed
  evidence and the data-restriction record
- the difficulty gap records, with their exclusion reasons and the v3
solver
  protocol
- the curation records: legacy source declarations kept exactly as main
defines them, a QualifiedSourceDeclaration with exact-pin validation
beside
  them, and the standalone evidence, measurement and census records

License receipts fail closed. Ingest and admission need evidence from
the
current resolver, bound to the exact source revision. A recorded ban, a
registry ban, or a restrictive classification blocks ingest, unless an
explicit exception decision covers it. The license policy tables and the
classifier move here from experiments/data_belay/intake.py. Data Belay
now
uses this module, so the two classifiers cannot drift. The shared table
also
widens the policy: DATA_LICENSES adds ODC-By 1.0 and the PDDL/ODC-PDDL
public-domain dedications. Data Belay intake now accepts datasets that
it
sent to review before.

commits.message:
[verifyit] Grade list replies whose members carry their own brackets (#11739)

A math LIST reply whose members carry their own brackets now grades as
the
same members as a reference written with outer brackets.

`_split_members` dropped a sequence's first and last characters whenever
they
read as an opener/closer pair, even when that pair did not enclose the
whole
text. A reply in HARDMath's polynomial_roots form `\left[…\right],
\left[…\right]`
lost its first `[` and last `]`, split into three members, and scored 0
against
its own LIST reference on all 65 polynomial_roots rows; the golden
control that
carries the outer brackets scored 1, so admission missed the false
negatives.
On main the same split scored `(1,2),(3,4)` 0 against the LIST reference
`[(1,2),(3,4)]`. The outer brackets are now dropped only when the first
opener
closes at the last character with the text between balanced, and the top
level
otherwise splits as is.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[skyrl] Quarantine prompts that only produce unusable groups (#11708)

The loader now counts unusable groups (`fully_masked` or
`below_minimum_group_size`) per prompt. After
`trainer.rollout_buffer.max_unusable_groups` in a row (default 3), it
quarantines the prompt: it does not offer the prompt for the next 10
training steps, logs a warning with the prompt and the last rejection,
and reports `async/quarantined_prompts`. The prompt then returns with a
fresh count. A usable group resets the count. Stale and duplicate-uid
rejections don't affect it.

A prompt whose grader fails on every sample is otherwise offered again
with no limit. With spare prompts, each pass spends a group on it.
Without spare prompts, the batch cannot fill and the run ends at the
admission stall timeout (30 minutes before the first step, later at
least 10), with an error that does not name the prompt.

Quarantine is temporary because infrastructure failures mask their
samples: a sandbox or verifier outage produces the same unusable groups
as a broken grader. For the same reason quarantine never leaves fewer
usable prompts than one batch needs. A prompt at that limit stays in
rotation and the loader logs a warning that names it; the stall timeout
remains the only failure path.

Truncated but graded samples still count toward the baseline, so prompts
the model cannot finish are not quarantined while
`apply_overlong_filtering` is off (the default). Quarantine is not
checkpointed; a resumed run starts with every prompt in rotation.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Worker batch assembly (3/3): Assemble batches on policy workers (#10668)

With `trainer.batch_builder=worker`, each policy worker builds its own data-parallel slice of the training batch and keeps it through the forward pass and the optimizer step. The driver sends only a plan of which rows go to which rank. The default stays `driver`, which gives the same training results as main. On checkpoint resume, both modes rebuild each restored group's row summary from its stored rollout. Both modes run on the Megatron backend and train only the policy; Megatron training does not support a critic model.

The driver holds only the plan, so its memory does not grow with the batch. On 8 H100s with a small model and a full-size batch (8,192 sequences, 98 million response tokens, responses up to 98,940 tokens), same rollouts and seed in both modes ([paired run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-worker-batch-sync-benefit-1113-a2), measured on an earlier commit of this branch; fixed stored rollouts with no generation, one run per mode, median of steps 2 and 3):

| | `driver` | `worker` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Driver process memory, peak | 144 GB | 1.9 GB |
| Pod memory, peak | 445 GB | 304 GB |
| Ray object store, peak | 110 GB | 11 GB |
| Training step, median | 3,084 s | 2,749 s |

Most of the step-time saving is in the policy-training phase (2,410 s to 2,179 s); the run's timers do not show which part of it. Batch assembly takes 24 s in worker mode and 51 s in driver mode.

Worker mode supports the outcome estimators (`rloo`, `rloo_n`, `grpo`) with the regular, dual-clip, GSPO, CISPO, SAPO, importance-sampling and behavior-clip losses, and SFT with uniform advantages, with scalar or per-turn token rewards. It refuses other settings at startup with a message that names the setting, and those runs use `driver`; the [dev guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9495bb6e3435cabc3e18425917e8d40b09023e8/docs/dev-guide/skyrl.md#batch-assembly) lists them. Worker mode reports summed and maximum mismatch metrics; the percentile, ESS, KL, chi-square and tail metrics and the standard deviation of the probability difference are driver-only.

Both modes give the same results in these tests:
- [H100 driver-vs-worker test](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-worker-batch-loom-snowball-1118-a1) (tiny mixture-of-experts model, pipeline and data parallel, router replay), which runs the trainer's step in each mode: every rank's inputs, the routes, the loss, the gradient norm and the updated parameters are identical in both modes. A one-off run of the same check at a tiny Mochi shape (latent attention, short convolution, two shared experts) was also identical ([run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-worker-batch-cuts-mochi-1116-a1), earlier commit).
- [CPU suite on this branch](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-worker-batch-loom-review-1118-a1): everything passes except two Daytona tests that fail the same way on main; the skipped tests need storage credentials and run in the nightly below. It includes two-step GRPO and SFT training in both modes with identical losses, gradient norms and metrics, and a worker resume that trains on restored groups. The 2,200-batch comparison from #10666 finds no difference from main.
- [Nightly CPU workflow with storage credentials](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44150608455) on an earlier commit of this branch: all tests pass, including the worker GRPO, SFT and resume tests. One driver-mode checkpoint-resume test passed on its second attempt, and main's nightly passed the same day.

A 64-H100 GSM8K run in worker mode completed two steps of 8,192 sequences on all ranks ([run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-worker-batch-marin-length2-gsm8k64-1106-a1), earlier commit).

Part of marin-community/MarinSkyRL#888

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[marina] Serve public named applet hosts from the public reader (#11690)

Named applet hosts must serve public-mode apps without Google sign-in,
but each host maps to the IAP-protected `marina` service.

Add `marin-marina:public_applet_domains`. Pulumi maps each host in this
list to the `marina-public-applets` service. Pulumi gives the list to
that service as `MARINA_APPLET_DOMAINS`. The public reader then resolves
the host in `marina.applet_hosts` and rewrites the request to the bound
app's `/a/<id>/` routes. These are the same GET and HEAD routes as the
app's `public.applets.marina.oa.dev` URL, so the content and headers are
the same. Hosts in `applet_domains` stay on the protected service.

The reader reads the app's stored mode on each request. An unbound host,
a disabled host, or a host bound to a private or archived app returns
404. Thus `marina apps mode UUID private` stops public service through
the host without a deploy. The protected service cannot delegate to the
public reader, because IAP rejects the request before it gets to the
container. Thus the service for each host is set at deploy time, and the
access check is done by the reader at request time. A public host does
not fall back to the protected service. The protected service also gets
the public hosts, so that operators can bind them with `marina apps
hosts bind`.

The stack config adds `atlas.oa.dev` to `public_applet_domains`. The
deploy creates one Cloudflare DNS-only CNAME (`atlas.oa.dev` to
`ghs.googlehosted.com`) and one Cloud Run domain mapping to
`marina-public-applets`. It also updates `MARINA_APPLET_DOMAINS` on both
services. There are no new secrets and no IAM or IAP changes. After the
deploy, an applet operator must bind `atlas.oa.dev` to the public RL
Data Atlas app.

Domain mappings ignore changes to their route. If a host moves between
`applet_domains` and `public_applet_domains`, remove it in one deploy
and add it to the other list in the next. A host cannot be in both
lists.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[skyrl] Preserve worker diagnostics without attached exceptions (#11621)

Preserve asyncio diagnostics without an attached exception in SkyRL
worker logs. Asyncio can emit `exc_info=False`; the stdlib-to-Loguru
bridge indexed it as an exception tuple, raised `TypeError` and lost the
original diagnostic. Treat it as no attached exception while retaining
real exception tracebacks.

A subprocess regression fails on main and passes with the repair. It
checks messages and worker IDs from asyncio's context dictionary, plus a
real exception's type, message and traceback frame. This repairs
diagnostic logging; it does not establish the cause of the original
worker failure.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[skyrl] Use standard NCCL buffers for policy and reference roles (#11656)

Megatron policy and reference roles now resolve to an explicit 4-MiB
NCCL SIMPLE buffer, and reference forwarding applies in dedicated and
colocated layouts. The previous reference default was 256 KiB; an unset
policy value delegated sizing to the runtime. The resolved settings
override an inherited small-buffer environment. Explicit role tuning
remains available. Colocated reference workers retain larger buffers, so
their memory budget must account for that.

NCCL 2.30.7 returned incorrect native C and ProcessGroupNCCL reductions
with a 256-KiB buffer. A source-library A/B reproduced the failure and
corrected it by bounding the NVLSTree chunk to its FIFO slot.
Existing-library 4-MiB controls passed the tested 16–512-MiB range;
1-MiB controls failed at 512 MiB. This mitigation keeps the existing
library and strict comparator. The eight-GPU A/B does not qualify every
topology or message size.

The regression captures resolved role environment mappings at actor
allocation with inherited NCCL_BUFFSIZE=262144. Existing immutable run
artifacts are unchanged; these defaults apply to future launches.

Part of #11649

[rl] Reject quick-loop selections smaller than one update (#11701)

A quick loop whose selection has fewer than 128 training tasks fails at
SkyRL's data load (`len(prompts_dataset) >= train_batch_size`). That
check runs only after the 40 GPUs are allocated and the model has
loaded.

An update trains each task at most once, so the selection needs at least
one batch of distinct rows. The launcher now reads the row count from
the `train.parquet` metadata and rejects a smaller selection before
submission, with the count and the required batch size.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[skyrl] Log the provider error when a task machine fails (#11704)

When a task machine or grader machine fails to start, the rollout worker
logs only `TaskMachineError`, and the rollout's diagnostics keep only
the provider's error type, HTTP status and SDK call. Daytona
`snapshot.get` HTTP 400 failures during grader creation therefore can't
be diagnosed: neither the log nor the saved rollouts contain Daytona's
error message, and the snapshot may be gone by the time anyone looks.

When the underlying error is a `DaytonaError`, the worker's warning now
includes its type and message, passed through
`rigging.redaction.redact_string` because provider text can contain
credentials. For example: `TaskMachineError (DaytonaValidationError:
Failed to get snapshot: ...)`. Redaction also masks high-entropy
identifiers such as snapshot names. Other providers' errors still log
only the exception type, and the persisted diagnostics keep their
allowlisted fields unchanged.

commits.message:
[rl] Force NCCL onto TCP in the Snowball quick loop (#11700)

The Snowball quick loop fails on cw-us-east-02a at the first inter-node
pipeline-parallel collective: NCCL logs `NET/IB: Got completion ...
status=IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR(12)` and then `ncclRemoteError`.

#11178 removed the TCP override because InfiniBand worked on the nodes
its smoke landed on. The fault from 2026-10-20 still occurs on other 02a
nodes, so a quick loop fails within minutes depending on placement.

Restore `NCCL_NET=Socket`, `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` and
`NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY=AF_INET` in the launcher's `extra_env`. With these
settings, the same 5-node layout completes model load, weight sync,
three updates and both evaluations. TCP weight sync costs about 7 s per
update (measured in #11178). Remove the override once the 02a InfiniBand
fault is fixed.

commits.author: HRL9000
commits.message:
[finelog] Record catalog min/max for flagged columns (#11394)

Record each segment's min and max for columns flagged `catalog_bounds`,
and flag `log.epoch_ms`. This is the write half of #11184, which will
use the bounds to skip segments in time-bounded queries. Part of #11172.

Nothing reads the bounds yet. Until #11184 lands, this PR only adds
cost: maintenance reads Parquet footers to backfill existing segments,
up to 64 segments per table per tick.

- `ColumnIndex.catalog_bounds` applies to INT64 columns only. When
schemas merge it can only turn on, never off, so a sender on an older
schema doesn't clear it on the hub. It is outside the index policy
fingerprint, so turning it on rebuilds no index.
- The bounds are stored in `object_segments.column_bounds`, the column
that catalog migration 0007 (#11579) added, and in the checkpoint's
`CatalogSegment.column_bounds`. NULL means no range is recorded. This PR
adds no migration.
- Flush, merge and spec migration record bounds for the segments they
write.
- The key-bounds maintenance task becomes `SegmentBounds`, which also
fills missing column bounds from footers without rewriting objects. It
mainly matters for L3, which is never rewritten. A column with no usable
statistics is recorded as always-scan, so the segment leaves the
backfill queue and queries still read it.

To roll out, deploy the new image once #11579 is deployed; nothing needs
to run by hand. Segments written from then on get bounds as they are
flushed or merged. From the first maintenance tick, the backfill adds
bounds to existing segments, 64 per table per tick, until every object
segment has them. Query results and plans don't change until #11184.

The #11579 image can be redeployed after bounds have been written. It
already knows migration 0007, so it opens the catalog, and everything
this PR writes goes where that image ignores it:

- That image never reads `object_segments.column_bounds`.
- The checkpoint JSON decoder ignores the new
`CatalogSegment.column_bounds` field.
- The `catalog_bounds` flag is a key in the namespace's stored schema
JSON, whose decoder doesn't reject unknown keys. It is also field 4 on
`ColumnIndex`, which protobuf ignores, so a client that sends the flag
to an older server is fine.

Segments that image writes get NULL, and checkpoints it rewrites drop
the bounds; after the next upgrade, the backfill restores them. This was
checked from the code; it has not been run end to end with the #11579
binary against a catalog this PR wrote.
